concepts.label: service memory quota
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - already promoted. This page is the fullest account of it: minimums, allocation rules, and the two exempt services.

concepts.label: bucket memory quota
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - sibling of server:service-memory-quota but a distinct axis: a per-bucket allocation carved out of the Data Service's own quota, not a per-service cluster-wide allocation. 'The available memory for a bucket comes from the quota you assign to the Data Service.'

concepts.label: ejection policy (eviction method)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - umbrella term for the closed per-bucket-type policy sets below. 'You assign an ejection policy (also known as an eviction method) to each bucket that determines if and how the Data Service ejects data from memory.'

concepts.label: Value-only ejection
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - default Couchbase-bucket policy; referenced as an object from buckets.json this batch.

concepts.label: Full ejection
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - sibling of memory:value-only-ejection.

concepts.label: No ejection (Ephemeral)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - Ephemeral-bucket policy, sibling family to the Couchbase-bucket policies above.

concepts.label: Eject data when RAM is full (Ephemeral, NRU-based)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - sibling of memory:no-ejection.

concepts.label: memoryLowWatermark
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the threshold at which ejection stops; renamed from the cbepctl-era mem_low_wat setting per this page's own note.

concepts.label: memoryHighWatermark
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - sibling of memory:memory-low-watermark; the threshold at which ejection starts.

concepts.label: warmup process
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the sequential disk-to-memory reload a node performs on restart.

concepts.label: warmupBehavior (background/blocking/none)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - closed three-member enum controlling memory:warmup-process, modeled as a scheme with a flat literal list on the same pattern as the registry's index-state, since no page references one of the three values as its own individually-linked concept.

concepts.label: access scanner
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the periodic process that identifies frequently-used keys and writes them to the access log consulted during warmup.

concepts.label: resident ratio
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the percentage of a bucket's active-and-replica-vBucket items currently held in memory on a node; the metric the access scanner evaluates.

concepts.label: Expiry Pager
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the process that scans for and erases expired items, leaving a tombstone; renamed from the cbepctl-era exp_pager_stime setting per this page's own note.

concepts.label: Active Memory Defragmenter
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the process that repacks sparsely-used memory pages to counter fragmentation from ejection and item resizing.

concepts.label: tombstone
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - extraction-layer, minted on storage-settings.json this batch (its dedicated Tombstones section); referenced incidentally here by the Expiry Pager.

relations.subject: memory:warmup-process
relations.evidence: The settings `warmup_min_items_threshold`, `warmup_min_memory_threshold`, and enabling access scanner are no longer supported through `cbepctl`. These settings are replaced by a new setting `warmupBehavior` and `accessScannerEnabled`, which can be configured using REST APIs.

relations.subject: memory:memory-low-watermark
relations.evidence: The settings `mem_high_wat`, and `mem_low_wat` are no longer supported through `cbepctl`. These settings are replaced by new settings `memoryLowWatermark` and `memoryHighWatermark`, which can be configured using REST APIs.

relations.subject: memory:memory-high-watermark

relations.subject: memory:expiry-pager

notable_absence.finding: This page states server:service-memory-quota is 'established by the Full Administrator' but never states which role (if any) is required to change an existing bucket's ejection policy or watermark settings later via the REST API - the Ejection and Memory Watermarks sections describe the mechanics in full but are silent on authorization, unlike memory-and-storage.md's neighbor buckets.md which does cross-reference Authorization explicitly for bucket security generally.

cross_component_finding: storage-engines.md and this page independently state the identical two figures (Couchstore: 10% minimum memory-to-data ratio; Magma: 1%) in near-identical wording ('minimum memory-to-data ratio of 10%' vs 'recommended to be at least 10% of your expected dataset size') - the same numbers, restated rather than cross-linked, is a real content-duplication pattern worth reconciliation's attention if either figure is ever updated in only one place. Separately, three unrelated settings on this single page - warmup_min_items_threshold/warmup_min_memory_threshold, mem_high_wat/mem_low_wat, and exp_pager_stime - are all stated as no-longer-supported-through-cbepctl and replaced by REST-API-configurable settings, a pattern specific enough (three independent renamedFrom instances on one page) to suggest a deliberate, cluster-wide migration away from cbepctl that the docs state piecemeal per-setting rather than as one architectural note.
